exit_criteria.text: Downloads a 1 GB file correctly over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2
exit_criteria.evidence: tests/corpus/tests/gigabyte.rs, run by `just corpus-slow`. Verified 2026-08-03: 1 000 000 000 bytes over HTTP/1.1 (3.0s) and over HTTP/2 as h2c (3.6s), each compared byte for byte against blake3-ctr-v1 with 0 mismatches. The verifier itself is proven able to fail by a companion test that flips one byte 3 MiB in. Caveat recorded as backlog B-8: HTTP/2 here is cleartext h2c, not h2 over TLS with ALPN, which the corpus cannot yet express.

exit_criteria.text: The capability probe correctly classifies range support on every 'ranges' corpus case
exit_criteria.evidence: 15 cases in tests/corpus/cases/ranges/, all passing, each asserting expect.range_support explicitly so the classification is checked rather than inferred from the download succeeding. They cover every range behaviour the pathology server can produce - correct 206, Accept-Ranges absent, Accept-Ranges lies, 206-with-whole-body, shifted Content-Range, omitted Content-Range, three malformed Content-Range shapes, unknown total length, multipart/byteranges for a single range, totals both overstated and understated - plus the proven path over h2c and with no validator and with a weak-ETag-only validator. Exactly one behaviour yields Proven; the other fourteen do not, and five of those answer with 206. HONEST LIMIT: the category is 15 against docs/09 section 3.2's initial target of 25. What is covered is every classification path the corpus can currently express; the remainder need features from later stages (multi-range requests, If-Range, CDN edge disagreement) and are tracked as B-13.

exit_criteria.text: Filename sanitisation passes its property tests including path-traversal cases
exit_criteria.evidence: crates/downpour-types/tests/filename_prop.rs::sanitised_name_is_always_exactly_one_normal_component - proptest over arbitrary char sequences asserting the result is exactly one Component::Normal, so it cannot escape the directory it is joined to; plus sanitise_is_idempotent, resolve_never_panics, and a 22-case table covering ../, absolute paths, Windows-style separators, NUL, control characters, the Windows reserved device names, trailing dots and spaces, and multibyte truncation. Proven end to end by tests/corpus/tests/download.rs::a_traversal_in_content_disposition_cannot_write_outside_the_target_directory, which asserts the written file's parent is the target directory.

exit_criteria.text: Never writes a body received with an unexpected Content-Encoding
exit_criteria.evidence: Four layers, each asserted independently. Header level: crates/downpour-types/tests/range_proof.rs::a_gzipped_range_response_is_rejected. Probe level: tests/corpus/tests/probe.rs::a_compressed_ranged_response_is_an_error_not_a_downgrade, which also asserts it is NOT downgraded to RangeSupport::Absent - conflating those would let the transfer proceed over bytes that do not correspond to the representation. Request level: ::the_probe_sends_accept_encoding_identity, asserted against the request the SERVER recorded rather than against our own code. Filesystem level: tests/corpus/tests/download.rs::a_compressed_body_is_never_written asserts the target directory is EMPTY afterwards - not even a .dppart - and crates/downpour-cli/tests/dp_add.rs asserts exit 1 with no file. Mutation-checked: deleting the Content-Encoding check turns the first two red. Also structural: no decompression feature is enabled on reqwest, so there is no code path that could inflate a body.

exit_criteria.text: 'redirects' and 'framing' corpus categories pass
exit_criteria.evidence: Both categories are at or over docs/09 section 3.2's target and every case passes under `just gate`. framing 17/15: gzip-on-range, brotli, uppercase and padded non-identity tokens, a list containing identity, identity accepted in uppercase and padded form, chunked, close-delimited, chunked-short-but-well-formed, chunked-missing-terminator, truncated body, truncated after one byte, wrong Content-Length, HTML-instead-of-file, zero-length representation, and a body with no HTTP/1.1 length signal over h2c. redirects 10/10: mixed-status chain, 303, 308, loop bounded by the hop limit, chain over h2c, chain ending at an origin without range support, redirect with no Location, redirect to an unusable Location, cross-host handoff, and a cross-host chain that keeps its intra-origin hops. The last two assert expect.crosses_origin, without which they passed even with the cross-origin wiring disabled.

exit_criteria.text: Zero silent corruption across the S1 corpus subset
exit_criteria.evidence: 42 corpus cases, 0 silent-corruption findings, and the detector is proven able to fire rather than merely observed passing: ServerSpec::corrupt_from makes the server return the right length with inverted content from 32 KiB on, and tests/corpus/tests/runner_self_test.rs::the_runner_detects_a_server_that_serves_corrupt_bytes asserts the runner reports SILENT CORRUPTION naming byte 32768. Mutation-checked: disabling the comparison turns exactly that test red. The comparison is imposed by the runner on every case and is not a key a case can set (ADR-0010). Broadest single statement: 1 000 000 000 bytes byte-exact over HTTP/1.1 and h2c via `just corpus-slow`. metrics.silent_corruption_findings is 0, which the validator treats as a release blocker if it ever is not.

tasks.title: Pathology server: deterministic PRNG content, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, and the ranges/framing/redirects behaviours
tasks.proof: tests/corpus/tests/content_generator.rs (12 tests) and tests/corpus/tests/pathology_server.rs (29 tests), 41 total. Determinism: the server serves exactly the generator's bytes over both HTTP/1.1 and h2c, two servers with the same seed agree, and both protocols produce identical bytes. Pathologies verified against a reference client (hyper for h2, a hand-written reader for h1 - deliberately not downpour-http, which would be circular): accept-ranges-absent, accept-ranges-lies, 206-with-whole-body, shifted Content-Range, omitted Content-Range, literal malformed Content-Range, unknown total length, 416, chunked, close-delimited, wrong Content-Length, mid-body truncation, gzip-on-range, redirect chains, redirect loops, keep-alive reuse, request recording on both protocols, and an HTML error page where a binary was expected. Mutation-checked: making Lies honour ranges, ignoring truncate_body_after, and always emitting a correct Content-Range each turn red exactly the tests that claim those pathologies and no others.

tasks.title: The TransferProtocol trait and the h1h2 backend over reqwest/rustls
tasks.proof: crates/downpour-http/tests/trait_object.rs (9 tests). TransferProtocol is object-safe: usable as Box<dyn>, held in a Vec<Box<dyn>>, and shared across four tokio tasks as Arc<dyn> - which is what ADR-0005 rests on, since the simulator is just another backend. A stub backend satisfies the trait with no reqwest type in any signature, proving the abstraction does not leak. H1H2Backend coerces to the trait object and reports capabilities that differ by transport mode, so the scheduler never needs a version check. RangeSink is append-only from a fixed base offset, refuses a write past its grant whole rather than partially, and does not write anything on refusal (I-2 precondition); sync reaches the target (I-1 commit point). SCOPE LIMIT, stated rather than implied: h1h2::probe and h1h2::fetch_range are written but have NO behavioural test coverage yet - nothing has exercised them against a server. That is S1-T8's job and S1-T8's proof, and no exit criterion may be marked met on the strength of this task.

tasks.title: Capability probe: ranged GET, redirect-chain capture, validator and digest capture, HTML-instead-of-file detection
tasks.proof: tests/corpus/tests/probe.rs (19 tests) against PathologyServer. I-6: a validated 206 is the only behaviour that yields RangeSupport::Proven, and all seven others yield Absent - including the five that answer 206 (correct Content-Range with the whole body, shifted Content-Range, omitted Content-Range, malformed Content-Range, unknown total length). I-5: a gzipped ranged response returns ProbeError::ContentEncoding rather than downgrading to Absent, and Accept-Encoding: identity is asserted on the request the SERVER recorded, not on our own code. I-8: every redirect hop including the submitted URL is recorded, and a loop hits TooManyRedirects with a bounded request count. Also: HTML-instead-of-file, 401/403/410 -> needs_refresh distinguished from 500/503 -> unexpected_status, weak-ETag classification, digest capture, Content-Disposition traversal sanitised to a single component, and the probe over h2c. Mutation-checked: downgrading the gzip case, removing Accept-Encoding: identity, and taking total_length from Content-Length on a 206 each turn red exactly the test that claims it. PROOF FIELD REVISED from the original 'corpus categories ranges and redirects pass under just corpus'. That was a decomposition error on my part: it made this task's proof depend on S1-T10's runner and S1-T11's case files, which are separate deliverables. The behaviour is proven here; expressing it as declarative YAML inventory is S1-T11's job, and exit criterion S1-C2 still requires those cases, so the criterion holds that line rather than this task.

tasks.title: Single-stream download: .dppart target, Content-Encoding rejection, verify length and coverage and digest, then atomic rename
tasks.proof: tests/corpus/tests/download.rs (14 tests). I-4 asserted on every failure path: the final name is never created unless the delivered length matches what the probe established, and the assertions check the directory listing rather than only the return value. A truncated body leaves content.dppart holding bytes that still match the generator, so a later resume can trust them. I-5: a compressed body produces no file at all, not even a .dppart, because the probe rejects it first. Byte-exactness against the generator over HTTP/1.1, h2c, chunked framing, a redirect chain, and a server without range support. Plus: a Content-Disposition traversal lands inside the target directory, an existing file is never overwritten, and a zero-length representation still produces a file. FOUND AND FIXED TWO ENGINE DEFECTS while writing these, both caught by the new tests, both with their regression test in this change (Gate D): (1) the probe treated 416 as fatal, so an empty representation - or any server that refuses bytes=0-0 - could not be downloaded at all; docs/03 section 2.1 says a non-206 means single stream, not failure, so the probe now re-asks without a Range. (2) a body that died before its declared Content-Length surfaced as an opaque transport error, losing both that it was a truncation and how many bytes arrived, which docs/03 section 7 needs for its retry policy; now reported as TruncatedBody, detected from the length already known rather than by matching the HTTP library's error shape.

tasks.title: Corpus runner: YAML case to server configuration to engine run to assertions, wired to `just corpus`
tasks.proof: tests/corpus/tests/runner_self_test.rs (6 tests) - the fail-closed proof ADR-0010 requires - plus tests/corpus/tests/corpus_cases.rs (4 tests) which runs the whole case set. The two that matter: the_runner_fails_a_case_whose_expectation_is_wrong feeds the runner a fixture claiming a gzipped ranged response completes, and asserts the runner REJECTS it; and the_runner_detects_a_server_that_serves_corrupt_bytes has the server return the right length with correct headers and inverted content from 32 KiB on, and asserts a SILENT CORRUPTION finding naming byte 32768. That second one required adding ServerSpec::corrupt_from, and it is the most important self-test in the project: without a server that can serve wrong bytes, the runner's byte comparison is only ever observed passing, which is indistinguishable from a comparison that never runs. Mutation-checked: disabling the corruption check turns exactly that test red. Also asserted: an unknown key is a hard error naming the key (not a dropped assertion), a failure case with no error_kind is rejected, an unimplemented generator name is rejected rather than falling back, and a case describing mid-transfer `behaviour` is rejected because the server cannot enact it until S2. the_recorded_case_count_matches_reality pins metrics.corpus_cases_total to the files on disk so it cannot drift into a number nobody checks. YAML crate: serde_norway, recorded in docs/14.
tasks.notes: YAML crate research done 2026-08-03 so it need not be repeated. serde_yaml is DEPRECATED - its latest release is literally version 0.9.34+deprecated, last updated 2024-03-25 - so it must not be used. Live options, verified against crates.io: serde_norway 0.9.42 (a maintained fork of serde_yaml by cafkafk, updated 2024-12, 8.5M downloads, drop-in serde integration); serde_yaml_ng 0.10.0 (another fork, updated 2024-05, 7.6M downloads); yaml-rust2 0.11.0 (updated 2025-12, 49M downloads, but a low-level parser with no serde derive support, so the case structs would be hand-parsed); saphyr 0.0.11 (yaml-rust2's successor, actively developed, but still 0.0.x). RECOMMENDATION: serde_norway, because ADR-0010 requires the runner to FAIL CLOSED on an unknown key, which serde's deny_unknown_fields gives directly - and a hand-rolled parser would have to reimplement exactly that. Record it in docs/14 section 1 rather than writing an ADR: the cases are plain YAML data, so any conformant parser can read them and the choice is cheap to reverse. Remember the fail-closed requirement is the point of the task: also needed are the tests/corpus/self-test/ fixture whose deliberately-wrong expectation must make the runner FAIL, and the unconditional byte-comparison and file_renamed assertions that no case may opt out of.

tasks.title: dp add <url>: single-stream download from the command line
tasks.proof: crates/downpour-cli/tests/dp_add.rs (7 tests) run the built dp binary as a subprocess, so argument parsing, the exit code, stdout and stderr are all under test - a library-level test would pass with a binary that never ran. Byte-compares the downloaded file against the generator over HTTP/1.1, h2c, and a server without range support; asserts exit 1 with an empty stdout and NO file created when the probe refuses a compressed body (I-5); asserts exit 1 and no final name when the body is truncated (I-4); asserts a bad URL is reported without touching the network; and asserts --version and --help work, which catches a clap misconfiguration that would otherwise first appear in front of a user. Also verified manually against a real python http.server: 3 MB downloaded byte-identical (cmp clean), exit 0, the path on stdout, then exit 1 with 'refusing to overwrite' on a re-run and exit 1 'answered 404' for a missing file. Test placement note: this lives in downpour-cli rather than tests/corpus because Cargo sets CARGO_BIN_EXE_dp only for integration tests in the binary's own package, and that is also what guarantees the binary was built first - from another package the path has to be guessed, and a guess that misses becomes a test that silently never ran the binary.

tasks.title: 1 GB correctness over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2
tasks.proof: tests/corpus/tests/gigabyte.rs::a_gigabyte_over_http11_is_byte_exact and ::a_gigabyte_over_http2_is_byte_exact, run by `just corpus-slow` (release, --run-ignored all). Verified 2026-08-03: 1 000 000 000 bytes over HTTP/1.1 in 3.0s and over h2c in 3.6s, both compared byte for byte against the generator with 0 mismatches. Neither side holds a gigabyte: the server generates each chunk as it is polled and the verifier streams the file past the generator 1 MiB at a time. A third test, NOT ignored, corrupts one byte deep in the third window and asserts the verifier panics - without it the two gigabyte results would prove nothing. Ignored by default so the every-push budget stays under five minutes (docs/09 section 6). REQUIRED A SERVER FIX: the pathology server materialised the whole body in memory, which made a 1 GB case impossible and silently capped the corpus at what fits in RAM. Both protocols now stream from the generator, which is the reason the generator was made seekable in the first place.

tasks.title: Migrate CI to GitHub Actions and fix the pipeline that burned 400 GitLab minutes
tasks.notes: Measured the old pipeline before changing it: 1706 s = 28.4 min billed per run, which is 14 runs per 400-minute quota. Root causes, all confirmed in the config rather than guessed: (1) `cargo install` appeared 6 times and ~/.cargo/bin was NOT in cache.paths, so cargo-nextest/deny/audit were recompiled from source in every job of every run - cargo-audit alone was 370-511 s because it pulls ~300 crates including aws-lc-sys (C++/cmake) and gix; (2) four separate Rust jobs each compiled the workspace, and `unit` ran nextest --workspace while `corpus` re-ran the same corpus tests with -p downpour-corpus, 633 s of pure duplication; (3) fmt and clippy shared a cache key within one stage and clobbered each other. Comparing three consecutive pipelines proved the cache achieved nothing: unit 671/599/440 s, corpus 639/432/634 s, audit 511/501/370 s, and clippy got SLOWER at 98/116/136 s. MEASURED RESULT (GitHub Actions, cold cache, run 30826183828): 146 s total across three jobs = 2.4 min, against GitLab's 1706 s = 28.4 min. A 91 percent reduction, and that is the COLD run. Step detail confirms every diagnosis: taiki-e/install-action took 0.0 s for cargo-nextest, the whole security job including cargo-deny and cargo-audit took 23 s against 370-511 s for audit alone on GitLab, and harness fell from ~35 s across three jobs to 8 s. Real work is now clippy 43 s plus nextest 51 s. The measurement also found a design mistake of mine: rust-cache's save step took 0.0 s because I had restricted save-if to master and develop, following advice written for repositories with many concurrent branches. On a single-maintainer project where nearly every push is to a feature branch, that makes every run cold. Removed. NEXT: measure a warm run to prove the cache actually restores, and get the new Windows job green.

risks.text: Silent corruption ships undetected because it is invisible in casual testing
risks.mitigation: Deterministic content generator gives ground truth per byte; crash injection at every write boundary; scorecard row 1 is a release blocker

risks.text: The Rust HTTP/3 stack stays experimental and cannot be shipped
risks.mitigation: TransferProtocol trait keeps h3 quarantined behind a feature flag; S6 may legitimately end with 'works, stays behind the flag'

risks.text: Browser extension store review rejects or delays the extension over native messaging and host permissions
risks.mitigation: Minimal permissions with written justification; no remote code; reproducible build from source; version skew handled by the IPC handshake

risks.text: Single-maintainer bandwidth: ten stages is a long road
risks.mitigation: Each stage produces something independently useful; the CLI is a shippable product from S3 onward

risks.text: AI agents produce plausible code that does not compose into a system
risks.mitigation: The harness: PROVE-before-BUILD, Gate A proof fields, Gate D corpus rule, machine-validated progress file

risks.text: The compatibility corpus is not maintained and the strategy quietly fails
risks.mitigation: Gate D is non-waivable: no fix lands without its case; corpus metrics tracked in this file

risks.text: Adaptive concurrency oscillates or underperforms a well-chosen fixed count
risks.mitigation: Dedicated simulation scenarios; ADR-0009 names the fallback (fixed count with learned per-origin defaults)

backlog.text: downpour-cli links downpour-http directly in S1 because no daemon exists yet. When downpour-daemon lands, move the transfer behind IPC so the architecture rule 'clients never link the engine' (docs/02 section 3) holds again.
backlog.rationale: Roadmap S1 lists only three crates, so a direct link is the only option now; recorded so it is not mistaken for the intended end state

backlog.text: The minimal file sink written in S1 (crates/downpour-http/src/sink.rs) is superseded by downpour-storage in S2, which owns preallocation, positional writes, the journal and the durability ordering (I-1, I-9, I-10).
backlog.rationale: S1-C6 needs verify-before-rename now, but S1 has no storage crate to put it in

backlog.text: S1 captures a server-supplied Repr-Digest/Content-Digest but does not verify it. S2 must verify a captured digest before the final rename (I-4), which needs base64 decoding and sha2. Until then, no S1 corpus case may supply a digest, or the engine would be ignoring evidence it holds.
backlog.rationale: docs/03 section 2.1 step 6 says record it; I-4 says check it when the server supplied one. S1 does the first half only, deliberately.

backlog.text: RangeProof deliberately does not derive Deserialize: a derived impl would be a second constructor that skips the validation, turning the compiler-enforced I-6 back into a convention. When S2 persists a RemoteObject it must either re-validate on load or store the raw observation and rebuild the proof from it.
backlog.rationale: The hazard is invisible at the point where someone will reach for #[derive(Deserialize)], so it is recorded rather than left to be rediscovered

backlog.text: The corpus serves plaintext HTTP/1.1 and h2c (prior knowledge), not TLS. docs/09 section 7 requires local offline tests and TLS would add certificate management for no S1 coverage: nothing in ranges, framing or redirects depends on it. ALPN negotiation, Alt-Svc and h2-over-TLS belong to the protocols category, so the corpus needs a TLS listener with a test-only CA by S5.
backlog.rationale: Recorded so that 'HTTP/2 works' is not later over-read as 'HTTP/2 over TLS with ALPN works'

backlog.text: HTTP/2 framing pathologies are not expressible through the current h2c server, which goes through hyper: hyper owns h2 framing, so a wrong Content-Length or a missing terminator cannot be emitted. The Framing enum documents itself as HTTP/1.1-only. If an h2-specific framing pathology is ever needed, it requires the h2 crate directly or a hand-rolled frame writer.
backlog.rationale: The limitation is invisible from the case side, so it is recorded rather than left to be rediscovered

backlog.text: CLOSED 2026-08-03: cross-host redirects are implemented. The runner starts a second PathologyServer for the content origin and sets redirect_final_target on the first, and cases assert expect.crosses_origin so the behaviour is actually pinned. Protocol downgrade (https to http) remains out of reach until B-8 gives the corpus a TLS listener.
backlog.rationale: Named in I-8's proof list, so it must be covered before S1 closes

backlog.text: CLOSED 2026-08-03: RangeBehaviour::MultipartByteranges serves a multipart/byteranges body for a single-range request, with no top-level Content-Range, and case ranges/multipart-byteranges-for-single-range asserts the engine declines to prove range support and still produces a byte-exact file. Mutation-checked.
backlog.rationale: Named in docs/09 section 3.2's ranges description; needed before S1-C2 can honestly be met

backlog.text: Invariant coverage accounting, corrected 2026-08-03 from an over-generous 5 to 3. FULLY covered by S1 tests: I-4 (verify before rename, asserted on every corpus case), I-5 (four layers, mutation-checked), I-6 (one of eight server behaviours proves range support). PARTIALLY covered, and must not be counted until their real proof exists: I-1 (the sync is plumbed and tested, but I-1's proof is crash injection at every write boundary - S2), I-2 (the sink is append-only and refuses writes past its grant, but disjointness needs the allocator - S3), I-3 (weak-ETag classification is tested, but refusing resume on a changed validator is S2), I-8 (the redirect chain is captured and tested, but the URL-refresh flow is S8). Not affected in S1: I-7, I-9 to I-14.
backlog.rationale: invariants_covered gets quoted as release evidence, so an inflated count is worse than a low one

backlog.text: The ranges corpus category is at 15 cases against docs/09 section 3.2's initial target of 25. Every classification path the corpus can currently express is covered, so the shortfall is pathologies needing features that do not exist yet: multi-range requests and multipart responses with more than one part (S3), If-Range and validator-conditional ranges (S2), CDN edge disagreement between HEAD and GET across two origins, and a proxy that strips Accept-Ranges (S8). Grow the category as those stages land rather than padding it with further malformed-header variants, which belong at the parser's unit layer per docs/09 section 1.
backlog.rationale: S1-C2 is met as worded but the category is not exhaustive; recording the gap keeps that visible

backlog.text: Third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to major versions (actions/checkout@v7, actions/upload-artifact@v7, Swatinem/rust-cache@v2, taiki-e/install-action@v2), which trusts the tag to keep pointing somewhere safe. Before CI ever produces release artifacts, pin every third-party action to a full commit SHA - ADR-0011's first reversal trigger. Also configure branch protection on GitHub (master: no direct push; develop: require the CI check), because the GitLab protection that ADR-0003's release story assumes does not carry across hosts.
backlog.rationale: Losing master protection in the move would be a silent regression in the release story

session_log.summary: S1-T6 through S1-T8. Pathology server: hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 (hyper would correct or refuse the exact framing pathologies the corpus needs) plus h2c via hyper, verified against a reference client for 17 distinct pathologies. TransferProtocol trait with object safety asserted directly, since ADR-0005 and the future simulator depend on it. RangeSink is append-only from a fixed base offset, so a backend has no API for choosing an offset at all - I-2 made structural before there is any concurrency to get it wrong. h1h2 backend with hand-followed redirects (I-8 needs the whole chain) and no decompression features enabled (I-5). Capability probe proven against the server: one behaviour yields Proven, seven do not, five of which answer 206. Everything mutation-checked. Found and corrected one silently no-op mutation script, which had produced a meaningless pass.

session_log.summary: S1-T9, T12, T13 plus a server rewrite. Single-stream download with verify-before-rename (I-4), which found TWO engine defects: the probe treated 416 as fatal, making an empty representation undownloadable, and a body that died before its declared Content-Length surfaced as an opaque transport error, losing the truncation and the byte count that docs/03 section 7's retry policy needs. Both fixed with their regression tests in the same change. `dp add <url>` works, verified both by subprocess tests and by hand against a real http.server (3 MB byte-identical, correct exit codes, refuses to overwrite, reports 404). The pathology server buffered whole bodies in memory, which made a 1 GB case impossible and silently capped the corpus at what fits in RAM; both protocols now stream from the generator. S1-C1 is met: 1 GB byte-exact over HTTP/1.1 (3.0s) and h2c (3.6s). 139 tests, 6 doctests, just gate green. Every behavioural claim was mutation-checked, and one mutation script was found to be silently no-op'ing, which had produced a meaningless pass.

session_log.summary: S1-T10 done, S1-T11 started. The declarative case format and runner are in, with serde_norway (serde_yaml is deprecated upstream) chosen specifically because ADR-0010's fail-closed requirement IS serde's deny_unknown_fields. The runner imposes the byte-for-byte corruption comparison and the file_renamed check on every case, and neither is a key a case can set. Added ServerSpec::corrupt_from so the corpus can prove its own corruption detector fires - the server now serves the right length with wrong content and the runner catches it at the exact offset; mutation-checked. 11 cases written across ranges, framing and redirects, all passing. 149 tests, 6 doctests, just gate green.

session_log.summary: CI VERIFIED GREEN on commit 0307050: all ten GitLab jobs passed, including unit, corpus, audit and secret-scan. Earlier pipelines had been cancelled by successive pushes (interruptible: true), so this is the first confirmed full-stage pass. Then grew the corpus from 11 to 30 cases and closed both server-side blockers: B-10 cross-host redirects (a second PathologyServer, wired by the runner) and B-11 multipart/byteranges. The notable finding is a test-quality one: the first cross-host case proved nothing, because chain length and filename are identical whether or not a chain leaves its origin, and a mutation disabling the cross-origin wiring still passed. Fixed with expect.crosses_origin, which compares authorities; the mutation now fails. Recorded in S1-T11's notes as guidance for every future case.

session_log.summary: S1-T11 done; S1 proposed for gate review with 13/13 tasks and 6/6 criteria. Corpus grew 30 to 42 cases: framing 17/15 and redirects 10/10 are at or over docs/09 target, ranges 15/25 is short and the gap is recorded as B-13 rather than padded. Added server support for redirect Location pathologies (omitted, unusable) and for omitting the chunked terminator, which covered three error variants that had no test at all. TWO CASES CAUGHT PROVING LESS THAN THEY CLAIMED, both by mutation rather than by review: the first cross-host redirect case passed with the cross-origin wiring disabled (chain length and filename are identical either way; fixed with expect.crosses_origin), and content-encoding-uppercase/padded passed under a case-sensitive untrimmed check, because a stricter check also rejects them - case folding and trimming can only be proved on the ACCEPT side, so identity-uppercase and identity-padded were added and the two descriptions corrected to stop overclaiming. Also corrected one expectation I had written before observing: a truncated chunked response is well-formed and short, so it is caught by verify-before-rename as `incomplete`, not by the transport as `truncated_body`.
